title.narrative: The Green Evolution: Pathways for Food System Transformation

description.narrative: Approximately 16.000 smallholder farmer households with one farmer from each household (40% women) which will be clustered into 575 Groups; 11.000 additional farmers reached out through climate information service; 4.200 Community members reached out through food system dialogues and food system analysis (50% Women); 50 food entrepreneurs (micro level)100 elected representatives (Member of Parliament, Member of Legislative Agency) and 400 bureaucrats from Department of Agriculture/Horticulture/Livestock/Fisheries/Rural Development/Nutrition from District, State and National Level;1000 extension workers from Agriculture/Horticulture/Livestock/Fisheries/Rural Development/Nutrition of District (India)/Upazila (Bangladesh)/Municipality (Nepal) or lower geographical units under state/national governments.610 students (50% women) and 135 civil society members (40% women) as influencers reached out through capacity building.Altogether, the program will reach out to approximately 35.345 individuals directly (13.355 in India, 11.695 in Bangladesh and 10.295 in Nepal).

Impact: To support the implementation of national pathways in Bangladesh, Nepal, and India towards equitable, resilient, and sustainable food systems. Program Goal: Local agroecological food systems in Bangladesh, India and Nepal are strengthened through improved policy frameworks, operational structures and multistakeholder cooperation at all levels.

The project aims to contribute to enabling conditions in 3 countries for scaling-up agroecology for improving climate change adaptation/mitigation in food and farm system through a comprehensive multistakeholder approach. Robust evidence will be created and informed to scaling up strategies and political processes at larger scales which will ultimately be facilitated by a knowledge hub supporting the transformation and to synergize stakeholders’ engagement to the regional level.
